{"id": "4441f95f-3958-4345-bf5a-692f329ceeb4", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "Isolated log lines usually mean the spans aren't being collected or aren't linked across hops. AgentCore emits OpenTelemetry traces, and you view them in CloudWatch. This is the setup, based on the AWS documentation.

**1. Enable CloudWatch Transaction Search (once per account and Region)**
- This is the most common reason traces are missing. Until it's on, AgentCore can't send trace and span data to CloudWatch.
- After you enable it, open Transaction Search in the CloudWatch console. You can also use the GenAI Observability dashboard to see the full execution graph for a request.

**2. Make sure the agent emits spans**
- **Hosted on AgentCore Runtime:** the runtime instruments your agent with OpenTelemetry automatically. The docs say no extra configuration is needed beyond Transaction Search. Check that your agent's `requirements` include the ADOT package (`aws-opentelemetry-distro`) if you deploy from your own container or code.
- **Hosted elsewhere (Lambda, ECS, EKS, EC2):** add the AWS Distro for OpenTelemetry (ADOT) SDK and your framework's instrumentation library, for example LangChain. Without these, you only get logs.

**3. Look in the right place**
- Spans go to the `spans` log stream in the agent's log group, `/aws/bedrock-agentcore/runtimes/<agent_id>-<endpoint_name>`. Agents that use the shared span destination write to the `default` stream in the `aws/spans` log group.
- Newer agents use unified observability. Agents created in supported Regions from July 20, 2026 get a single per-agent log group that holds traces, prompts, structured logs and stdout. Existing agents can opt in by setting `UNIFIED_TRACES_DESTINATION_ENABLED=true` and upgrading ADOT to 0.17.1 or later. That puts logs and traces in one place, so correlating them is much easier.

**4. Propagate trace context across hops**
- Traces break up when a caller, tool or downstream service doesn't pass the trace header along.
- Pass `X-Amzn-Trace-Id` (X-Ray format) or `traceparent` (W3C format) on calls into the agent and through anything it calls. That includes API calls, SQS, SNS and EventBridge messages, and calls to MCP servers or gateways.
- AgentCore supports trace context propagation and custom ADOT instrumentation through its X-Ray integration.

**5. Tie logs to traces**
- Put `trace_id`, `session_id` and `agent_id` in your structured logs. Then you can pivot from a log line to its trace, or the reverse, with a Logs Insights query.
- Pass a consistent session ID on each invocation so that multi-turn requests group together.

If Transaction Search is on and you still see only log lines, the usual causes are:
- The ADOT SDK or framework instrumentation is missing, or its version is too old.
- Sampling is set too low.
- The agent's execution role can't write to CloudWatch or X-Ray.
- An upstream caller isn't forwarding the trace header.

I can check your AgentCore runtime configuration, log groups and Transaction Search status if you give me the Region and agent name. I'd also need to know whether the agent runs on AgentCore Runtime or on other compute.

Sources: [AgentCore and X-Ray](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/xray/latest/devguide/xray-services-agentcore.html), [View observability data for AgentCore agents](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/observability-view.html), and the AgentCore unified observability announcement.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
